title: Copper cold plates could slash data-center energy usage
publisher: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (MechSE news; Cell Reports Physical Science paper)
summary: University of Illinois (Miljkovic group) topology-optimised the fins of a pure copper liquid cold plate and had it built by Fabric8's electrochemical additive manufacturing, with detail down to 30-50 µm. Measured against conventional rectangular fins, it gave up to 32% better cooling, or up to 68% lower pressure drop at the same cooling. The researchers estimate a 1 GW AI facility would spend about 11 MW on cooling with these plates against 550 MW with air (an estimate, not measured). Published in Cell Reports Physical Science; US DOE funded.
thermal: Topology-optimised pure copper fins in a liquid direct-to-chip cold plate, reported at up to 32% better cooling and up to 68% lower pressure drop than conventional rectangular fins.
manufacturing: Pure copper fins built by electrochemical additive manufacturing (ECAM), which deposits copper layer by layer by electroplating, with features down to 30 to 50 micrometres; the fabricated part was imaged by SEM.

title: Why Two-Phase Direct-to-Chip Cooling is Reaching a Tipping Point
summary: Modelon blog based on an interview with Lingnan Lin and Kagan Sears of the University of Maryland on two-phase direct-to-chip cooling and transient system simulation. It cites rack power rising from 40-60 kW (H100, 2022) to 120-140 kW (Blackwell, 2024) and an expected 200-240 kW in 2026. No data; results are to be presented at the Purdue Herrick conferences. Opinion.
thermal: Two-phase direct-to-chip cooling that absorbs heat by boiling at the chip interface, with transient system simulation of the cold plate, working fluid, pumps and heat-rejection hardware for AI/HPC racks.

title: Design and evaluation of an additively manufactured aircraft heat exchanger
summary: Penn State compared a conventional brazed plate-fin aircraft oil cooler (CT-scanned to copy its internals) with two laser powder bed fusion AlSi10Mg copies, one with added air-side features. Measured heat transfer rose about 10% and 14%, but air-side pressure drop doubled, and the printed parts were rough with some cracks at fin-tube joints at the edges. Applied Thermal Engineering vol. 138, 2018. Older, but one of the few measured like-for-like tests of a printed aircraft oil cooler.
thermal: Plate-fin air-liquid crossflow heat exchanger (aircraft oil cooler) with overall heat transfer about 10% higher for the baseline AM design and 14% higher for the enhanced AM design, and measured air-side pressure drop about double the conventional unit.
manufacturing: Laser-based powder bed fusion of AlSi10Mg aluminium-alloy powder, with the conventional unit characterised by 3D X-ray CT; as-built parts showed significant surface roughness and some edge cracks in fin-tube joints.

title: Evaluation of Thermal Performance of the Motor Generator Unit-Kinetic (MGU-K) for 2026 Formula 1 Power Unit Regulations
publisher: SAE International (SAE Technical Paper 2025-01-8007, WCX SAE World Congress Experience)
summary: SAE paper 2025-01-8007 by Bayram and Samuel (Oxford Brookes) modelling MGU-K heat losses under the 2026 F1 power unit rules versus 2024, validated against 2023 qualifying data, with lumped-parameter plus finite element thermal models and proposed cooling specifications. Simulation; only the abstract was readable. Same paper as the Oxford Brookes repository item already on a card.
thermal: Thermal analysis of an F1 MGU-K electric motor under 2026 energy recovery and deployment rules, using lumped-parameter networks plus finite element thermal analysis, with proposed cooling specifications.

title: Laser-engineered copper surfaces for confined boiling and a thin wick-free vapour chamber (FFHMT 2026 paper 205)
summary: University of Ljubljana researchers (Hadžić, Golobič and colleagues) laser-textured copper surfaces and tested them in confined pool boiling and in a 1 mm thick wick-free vapour chamber. They report critical heat flux up to 118% higher and heat transfer coefficient at CHF up to 803% higher than untreated copper, and a vapour chamber resistance of 1.18 K/W at 40 W. Measured, lab scale, conference paper.
thermal: Laser-textured copper boosts boiling heat transfer in confined gaps and a thin vapour chamber for electronics.
manufacturing: Nanosecond-laser surface texturing of copper; vapour chamber without a sintered wick.

title: Cooling solution reduces thermal constraints, weight and size of commercial plane components
publisher: CORDIS (Publications Office of the European Union), European Commission; Results in Brief for the H2020 project TOPMOST
summary: CORDIS results brief for Clean Sky 2 project TOPMOST (2017-19, €712k), coordinated by NLR: a pumped two-phase cooling loop for aircraft power electronics. The demonstrators weighed 2.5 kg, were 42% smaller than required, cooled 2,400 W (twice the requirement) and held hotspots within 2 °C, and passed vibration and salt-spray tests. Most parts were 3D printed in aluminium. Project-reported results.
thermal: Two-phase pumped cooling loop in which a pump circulates fluid through an evaporator, using latent heat, to cool aircraft power electronics for more-electric aircraft at 2 400 W with hotspot spread below 2 °C.
manufacturing: Most components were 3D printed in aluminium, which the page describes as new for 3D printing, with the project expected to generate lessons on printing this metal; no process details are given.

title: Adapting Automotive Fuel Cell Technology for Next-Generation VTOL Light Aircraft: Challenges and Opportunities
publisher: The Vertical Flight Society (SAE Mobilus listing, product code F-0082-2026-0221)
summary: Vertical Flight Society 2026 forum paper by FEV Europe, FEV Group and RWTH Aachen arguing that automotive and heavy-duty fuel cell systems can be adapted for eVTOL light aircraft, which need much higher specific power. The abstract stresses that all waste heat goes through the cooling system and that bigger radiators add both mass and drag. Abstract only; no data.
thermal: Fuel cells must reject all waste heat through coolant systems and radiators, so compact, efficient radiator designs are needed because larger radiators add mass and drag.
manufacturing: Discusses adjusting fuel cell stack design and system architecture to meet eVTOL power-density requirements; no manufacturing process is described in the abstract.

title: Design of Ducted Heat Exchanger for Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell on Electric Aircraft
publisher: IEEE (Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Inc.), in 2025 IEEE/AIAA Transportation Electrification Conference and Electric Aircraft Technologies Symposium (ITEC+EATS 2025), Anaheim, 18-20 June 2025
summary: University at Buffalo, Georgia Tech and Florida State modelled megawatt-level heat rejection from a PEM fuel cell on an electric aircraft through a ducted heat exchanger, covering heat flux, drag, specific cooling power and pumping power across flight phases. The duct worked for most phases but could not reject enough heat at takeoff (little ram air, hot ground), so they propose a hybrid fuel cell plus turboelectric system. IEEE ITEC+EATS 2025; simulation, no numbers in the abstract.
thermal: MW-level heat rejection for a PEM fuel cell on an electric aircraft using a ducted heat exchanger, with cooling drag and pumping power analysed and a hybrid fuel cell plus turboelectric generator needed for takeoff.
manufacturing: Design study: the model sets the duct inlet to radiator core size ratio to optimise drag, cooling power and volume; no fabrication or physical test is described.

title: Challenges in Cooling Required for Fuel Cells in Aviation Applications

summary: AIAA Aviation 2024 paper from the same Buffalo, Georgia Tech, Florida State and Illinois Tech group comparing two ways to dump fuel cell heat on aircraft: ducted radiators and outer-mould-line (skin) heat exchangers, with heat flux and added drag for the IZEA concept aircraft. Abstract only; no figures.
thermal: Heat dissipation of high-power hydrogen fuel cell stacks on aircraft, comparing ducted radiators and outer mold line heat exchangers in terms of thermal flux and drag.
manufacturing: Proposes possible fuel cell and cooling system designs for aviation; no fabrication or test is described in the abstract.
